extracted.intended_audience: academics and researchers asked to peer review manuscripts for Elsevier journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for academics/researchers on whether to accept a review, how to evaluate different manuscript components (original research, reviews), ethical requirements, and how to write the review report for Elsevier journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise match
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the article match your area of expertise?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept only if capable of providing quality feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose any potential issues to the editor when responding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have any potential conflicts, report them to the editor rather than accepting/continuing without disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time commitment and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure you can meet deadlines; reviewing requires substantial work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly about availability; critical timing: respond promptly, even with a decline, because delays harm authors and slow the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge/training readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of your knowledge gaps and seek training where needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access free tutorials through Elsevier's Researcher Academy, including the 'Certified Peer Reviewer course' if you need to build reviewing skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy familiarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Review official reviewer responsibilities and guidelines before accepting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with journal- and publisher-specific policies that affect reviewer behavior and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat all materials as confidential; do not share without editor authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to manuscripts, reports, and correspondence about submissions. Maintain confidentiality throughout the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not upload the manuscript or any part of it into a Generative AI tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional prohibitions include: don't use AI on review reports or decision letters; don't employ AI for review evaluation or decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title & Abstract evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the title accurately and sufficiently describes the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the abstract summarizes the paper's aim, methods, key results, and conclusions appropriately and accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess current literature, scientific rationale, and clearly stated objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify whether the introduction sets the context, identifies gaps, and states clear aims or hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify sufficient detail for replication and appropriate experimental design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check description of patient/population selection, experimental procedures, and that statistical reporting is adequate; flag missing detail that prevents replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical reporting within Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess adequacy of statistical reporting in methods and analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure appropriate statistical tests are used and reported (e.g., sample sizes, models, assumptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Results presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Check presentation appropriateness and whether additional analyses are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend additional analyses where appropriate (confidence intervals, sensitivity tests) and ensure results are reported clearly and completely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure interpretation connects to data and limitations are explicitly emphasized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that claims are supported by findings, alternative explanations are considered, and limitations are stated and discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: References relevance and currency
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm that cited literature is relevant and up to date for the topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note missing key references or over-reliance on outdated sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate language quality and recommend professional editing if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest language/formatting improvements when clarity is impaired, but avoid making excessive comments on minor grammar (see DON'Ts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall assessment (novelty and impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine novelty, importance, and contribution to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an overall impression of whether the manuscript advances knowledge and is suitable for the journal's audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review articles evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess review articles for rationale, scope, and synthesis quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate: rationale for the review, historical development and future directions, coverage of recent/relevant research, methodological transparency (search strategies, inclusion criteria), appropriate statistical methods if applicable, overall structure and clarity, and language quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex and gender reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether studies include sex-disaggregated data and analyze gender appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend following SAGER guidelines and use consistent terminology: 'sex' for biological classification and 'gender' for socially constructed roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research data and ethics checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine data visualizations, figures, and tables and verify ethical approval documentation when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For studies involving human or animal subjects, check for documented ethical approval and appropriate reporting of consent and approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize the article briefly
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin the review with a brief summary demonstrating comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A short synopsis shows you understood the work and frames subsequent comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide main impressions regarding novelty and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: State your overall impressions about novelty and importance early in the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps editors and authors quickly understand your high-level judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use short, clearly-defined paragraphs referencing specific sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure comments in short paragraphs that reference manuscript sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This improves readability and helps authors locate issues to address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify journal-specific formatting compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether the manuscript complies with the target journal's formatting and submission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag noncompliance (e.g., word limits, reference style) but focus content-based review first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give specific, actionable suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide concrete, actionable recommendations for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague critiques; indicate what should be done and, where helpful, how to do it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review methodology, statistics, results, and conclusions carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Thoroughly evaluate the rigor of methods, correctness of analyses, and whether conclusions are supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out methodological flaws, statistical errors, or over-interpretation of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider data presentation and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess data presentation quality and whether the work is reproducible from the information provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check figures/tables for clarity, data availability statements, and whether sufficient detail exists to reproduce analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report suspected plagiarism or research misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Report suspected plagiarism or research misconduct to editors with detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include allegations in the public comments to the author; provide evidence and details to the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and mitigate unconscious bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of potential unconscious bias that may affect assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect on your own biases and avoid unfair dismissal of work for reasons unrelated to scientific merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't focus on minor grammar or spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not comment extensively on minor grammar or spelling issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor language errors should not dominate the review; recommend professional editing only if language impedes understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't make personal attacks or ad hominem remarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid personal attacks on authors or ad hominem language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep criticism objective and directed at the work, not the authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't dismiss alternative viewpoints without scientific reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not dismiss alternative viewpoints lacking genuine scientific reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique should be evidence-based rather than based on preference for particular theories or methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't share reviews without editor and author agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not share review contents without permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain confidentiality and follow journal policies on sharing reviews and manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't suggest citations solely to promote your own work
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid recommending citations that only serve to promote your own publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested citations should be genuinely relevant and improve the manuscript; disclose self-citation if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation types and editor's role
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide one of four recommendation options to the editor: Reject; Accept without revision; Revise (Major or Minor); or leave final decision to editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommending revision, specify required changes and indicate willingness for follow-up review; note that editors make the final decision and recommendations guide but don't determine outcomes.
